notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Admitted with complaints of fatigue, swelling in ankles, and shortness of breath on exertion. History of hypertension for 10 years, on Amlodipine 5mg. Suspecting early-stage CKD, ordering renal panel.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, slightly elevated. eGFR 58.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, up from 1.4 yesterday. Flag for review.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Reviewed rising creatinine trend. Adjusting fluid management, holding ACE inhibitor, nephrology consult requested. Continue monitoring daily.

notes.author: Dr. Nair
notes.text: Presented with fever, dry cough, and body ache for 3 days. No travel history. Advised CBC and chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: WBC count 11,200/uL, mildly elevated indicating possible infection.

notes.author: Dr. Nair
notes.text: Chest X-ray shows mild left lower lobe infiltrate consistent with early pneumonia. Started on Azithromycin 500mg once daily for 5 days.

notes.author: Nurse Rao
notes.text: Patient reports fever resolved, cough improving. Vitals stable. Tolerating oral antibiotics well.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Known Type 2 diabetic for 15 years, on Metformin and Glimepiride. Admitted for poor glycemic control and a non-healing ulcer on the left foot.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: HbA1c 9.8%, poor long-term glucose control.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Random blood glucose 286 mg/dL.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Started insulin sliding scale. Wound care team consulted for foot ulcer, debridement scheduled. Diabetic diet counseling initiated.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Random blood glucose improved to 162 mg/dL after insulin regimen.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: First prenatal visit, 12 weeks gestation. No prior pregnancies. No significant medical history. Prescribed folic acid and iron supplements.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, mild anemia for pregnancy stage.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Advised increased iron-rich diet, follow-up in 4 weeks with repeat CBC.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Admitted following a fall at home. X-ray confirms fracture of the left hip neck. History of osteoporosis, on calcium and vitamin D supplements.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Underwent hip hemiarthroplasty. Surgery uneventful. Post-op pain managed with scheduled analgesics.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL post-surgery, mild drop from baseline 11.5.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Hemoglobin drop attributed to surgical blood loss, within expected range. Transfusion not required. Starting physiotherapy tomorrow.

notes.author: Nurse Rao
notes.text: Patient mobilizing with walker, tolerating physiotherapy sessions well. Pain controlled.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Complains of recurrent migraines, 3-4 episodes per week over the last 2 months, affecting work. No aura. Family history of migraine present.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Started on Propranolol 40mg daily for prophylaxis. Advised migraine diary and trigger avoidance. Follow-up in 3 weeks.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Known hypertensive and smoker, presented with crushing chest pain radiating to left arm. ECG shows ST elevation in anterior leads.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Troponin I 4.8 ng/mL, markedly elevated, consistent with acute MI.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Emergency PCI performed, stent placed in LAD. Patient stable post-procedure, moved to CCU for monitoring.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Troponin I down to 0.9 ng/mL, trending toward normal.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Patient stable, started on dual antiplatelet therapy and statin. Cardiac rehab counseling provided. Planning discharge in 2 days.

notes.author: Dr. Nair
notes.text: Brought in by parents with high fever, rash on trunk, and irritability for 2 days. No known allergies. Query viral exanthem vs measles.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Temperature 39.4C recorded at triage.

notes.author: Dr. Nair
notes.text: Rash pattern and vaccination history reviewed, consistent with viral exanthem, not measles. Supportive care advised, antipyretics as needed.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Long-standing COPD patient, admitted with worsening breathlessness and productive cough. On home oxygen 2L/min.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Oxygen saturation 88% on room air at admission.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Started on nebulized bronchodilators, oral steroids, and controlled oxygen therapy. Sputum culture sent.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Oxygen saturation improved to 94% on 2L oxygen.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Clinical improvement noted, breathlessness reduced. Planning step-down to ward and discharge in 2 days with adjusted inhaler regimen.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Presents with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and intolerance to fatty food for 1 week. Ultrasound ordered to rule out gallstones.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Ultrasound confirms multiple gallstones with mild gallbladder wall thickening, no signs of acute cholecystitis currently.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Advised elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Patient counseled on low-fat diet in the interim. Surgery scheduled for next week.

notes.author: Dr. Nair
notes.text: College student presenting with sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and swollen tonsils for 2 days. No prior similar episodes.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Rapid strep test positive.

notes.author: Dr. Nair
notes.text: Diagnosed with streptococcal pharyngitis. Started on Penicillin V for 10 days. Advised rest and fluids.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Annual health checkup. Mild hypertension noted on repeat readings. No symptoms. Family history of cardiovascular disease.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Blood pressure 148/94 mmHg, LDL cholesterol 162 mg/dL.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Advised lifestyle modification, low-sodium diet, and started low-dose antihypertensive. Repeat lipid panel in 3 months.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Admitted with confusion and reduced oral intake over 3 days, reported by family. History of mild dementia, hypertension, and prior UTIs.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: Urinalysis shows significant leukocytes and nitrites, consistent with urinary tract infection.

notes.author: Dr. Mehta
notes.text: Started on IV antibiotics for UTI with likely delirium secondary to infection. IV fluids for rehydration.

notes.author: Nurse Rao
notes.text: Confusion improving, patient more oriented and taking oral fluids well. Family updated on progress.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Presents with lower back pain radiating to left leg for 2 weeks, following heavy lifting at work. No red-flag symptoms.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text: Clinical exam consistent with lumbar disc strain/mild sciatica. Advised NSAIDs, physiotherapy, and activity modification. MRI deferred unless symptoms worsen.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Known hypothyroid on Levothyroxine, presenting with fatigue and weight gain despite medication compliance.

notes.author: Lab
notes.text: TSH 9.2 mIU/L, elevated indicating under-treatment.

notes.author: Dr. Verma
notes.text: Increased Levothyroxine dose from 75mcg to 100mcg. Repeat TSH advised in 6 weeks.
